You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Corning Q2 Earnings Preview: AI Optical Communications Driving the Shift from Traditional Glass to Data Center Backbone

TEXT:
1. Investment Highlights at a Glance
Corning ( GLW ) is scheduled to report Q2 2026 results before the U.S. market open on July 28, 2026. Wall Street expects revenue of approximately $4.63 billion (+14.45% YoY), with core EPS in the $0.73–$0.77 range (around +25% YoY), broadly in line with company guidance. The market’s primary focus is whether the Optical Communications segment can sustain the strong momentum from Q1 and whether partnerships with NVIDIA , Amazon and other hyperscalers will translate into durable capacity and profit expansion. Current valuation already partially reflects the AI infrastructure narrative, so post-earnings volatility could be elevated.
2. Four Key Focus Areas
Focus 1: Optical Communications Growth and Contribution
Optical Communications has become the company’s primary growth engine. In Q1 the segment delivered +36% year-over-year sales growth and accounted for roughly 44.6% of total revenue. The market expects Q2 Optical Communications revenue to reach a new record, driven by AI data-center fiber, high-density interconnects and CPO architecture demand. Sustained growth above 25% would support overall revenue target s and reinforce confidence in the multi-year growth trajectory.
Focus 2: Progress on Long-Term Hyperscaler Agreements
In May, NVIDIA committed $500 million via warrants to secure capacity, prompting Corning to build three new U.S. factories with a target of 10× expansion in optical connectivity capacity and more than 50% growth in fiber capacity. In June, Amazon signed a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar supply agreement for optical fiber, cable and connectivity solutions, supporting expansion of North Carolina facilities and the creation of approximately 1,000 manufacturing jobs. These deals validate demand, but investors will watch the pace of order conversion and capacity ramp in Q2.
Focus 3: Gross Margin and High-Value Product Mix
Profitability has been improving since 2022. Q1 gross margin stood at approximately 36.9% with net margin near 10% . A rising mix of Optical Communications and higher-value connectivity products could further expand margins. At the same time , the Solar business is expected to incur roughly $30 million in additional costs related to maintenance and upgrades, which will temporarily pressure overall profitability.
Focus 4: Guidance and Free-Cash-Flow Outlook
Investors will closely monitor any updates to Q3 and full-year core sales and EPS guidance, as well as the impact of capital expenditure and customer prepayments on free cash flow. Reaffirmation or upward revision of the longer-term “Springboard” targets would further strengthen the AI infrastructure narrative.
3. Risks and Opportunities
Upside Catalysts:
Accelerating AI data-center buildouts driving Optical Communications orders above expectations;
New capacity coming online smoothly and converting quickly into revenue and higher margins;
Additional hyperscaler commitments or expanded long-term agreements improving multi-year visibility.
Downside Risks:
Solar-related costs exceeding expectations and weighing on EPS;
Slowdown in hyperscaler capital spending or supply-chain constraints limiting shipments;
Elevated valuation leaving limited room for error even if results merely meet consensus.
4. Trading Strategy Considerations
Bull Case: Optical Communications growth meaningfully exceeds guidance, margins improve, and management raises full-year outlook — reinforcing the AI infrastructure thesis and supporting further upside.
Bear Case: Results only meet expectations, Solar costs surprise to the upside, or management sounds cautious on second-half demand — potentially triggering profit-taking.
Key Metrics to Watch: Core revenue and EPS, Optical Communications segment sales and growth rate, gross-margin trajectory, and Q3/full-year guidance.
Positioning Notes: Ahead of the release, monitor implied volatility and the historical post-earnings pattern (roughly 50% probability of a positive next-day move over the past 12 reports). A clear beat plus constructive guidance could favor buying dips; a pure “in-line” outcome amid rich valuation may warrant tighter position sizing or waiting for a pullback.
